rules.sentence: Perineal lacerations are graded from first degree (interruption of vaginal mucosal only) to fourth degree (injury comprising the vaginal mucosa, pelvic floor muscles, external and internal anal sphincters, and the rectal mucosa).
Even after repair, lacerations often lead to pain, dyspareunia (pain with intercourse), pelvic floor dysfunction, and mood concerns.[1]

Third and fourth degree lacerations involve obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASI) and pelvic floor injuries of the levator ani muscles, which can lead to long term pelvic floor dysfunction including urinary or fecal incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse.[2]
